source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 15 Railroad Benefit (PDF p.22 Line 15; DR 0104AD p.2 line 15); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 30,000.00 + railroad retirement (RRB-1099-R) paid by the federal government (you) 20,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 32,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 32,250.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 50,000.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 32,250.00. DR 0104AD: Line 15 railroad benefit: railroad retirement included in federal taxable income 20,000.00 (no cap or age test). Line 22 subtotal = 20,000.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 20,000.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 32,250.00 - 20,000.00 = 12,250.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 12,250.00 = 539.00 (the tax table row over 12,200.00 but not over 12,300.00, PDF p.34, gives 539.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 539.00. Railroad retirement (Tier II, on Form RRB-1099-R) is subtracted in full on line 15; it is not also put on line 4, and with no other pension income line 4 is 0.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.
